bougie:Hostellerie de Levernois.name: Hostellerie de Levernois
bougie:Hostellerie de Levernois.label: RELAIS & CHÂTEAUX
bougie:Hostellerie de Levernois.hook: A Relais & Châteaux park, a Michelin-starred table, a Burgundy garden
bougie:Hostellerie de Levernois.text: A Relais & Châteaux park, a Michelin-starred table, a Burgundy garden EUR 250+ room BOOK-AHEAD Dinner A manor in a wooded park five minutes from the ramparts, with La Table de Levernois — one Michelin star under Philippe Augé, ex-Ducasse — and a kitchen garden that feeds it. The grand-gesture address of the Beaune area, and the quiet one: you hear the stream, not the town. Where Levernois — 5 km east of Beaune

bougie:Hôtel le Cep.name: Hôtel le Cep
bougie:Hôtel le Cep.label: FIVE STAR
bougie:Hôtel le Cep.hook: A five-star hôtel particulier in the cellar quarter, named for the vine
bougie:Hôtel le Cep.text: A five-star hôtel particulier in the cellar quarter, named for the vine EUR 230+ room BOOK-AHEAD All day A cluster of 16th- and 17th-century courtyards on rue Maufoux, each room named for a Côte d'Or climat. Le Bistro de l'Hôtel — the whole-roast-poularde room — and a spa beneath the old stone. Beaune's address for staying inside the walls in real comfort. Where Rue Maufoux

bougie:Hostellerie Cèdre & Spa.name: Hostellerie Cèdre & Spa
bougie:Hostellerie Cèdre & Spa.label: FIVE STAR
bougie:Hostellerie Cèdre & Spa.hook: A 19th-century mansion under a great cedar — and a Michelin star
bougie:Hostellerie Cèdre & Spa.text: A 19th-century mansion under a great cedar — and a Michelin star EUR 260+ room BOOK-AHEAD Dinner A bourgeois mansion on the ring boulevard, the cedar in the garden giving it its name and its starred restaurant, Clos du Cèdre, its address. Five-star, walled-garden calm, two minutes from Place Carnot. Where Boulevard Maréchal-Foch

dish:Œufs en meurette.name: Œufs en meurette
dish:Œufs en meurette.label: TRADITIONAL
dish:Œufs en meurette.hook: Eggs poached in red wine — the dish where the appellation is the sauce
dish:Œufs en meurette.text: Eggs poached in red wine — the dish where the appellation is the sauce EUR 12-18 WALK-IN Lunch Eggs poached gently in a reduction of Pinot Noir — the meurette sauce — finished with lardons, button mushrooms and a small onion garnish, served on a garlic-rubbed croûton. This is the cathedral dish of Beaune: the plate where you taste the slope in a breakfast egg, where wine is not the pairing but the medium. Order it at Le Bistrot Bourguignon or Loiseau des Vignes . Where every honest bouchon

dish:Bœuf bourguignon.name: Bœuf bourguignon
dish:Bœuf bourguignon.label: TRADITIONAL
dish:Bœuf bourguignon.hook: Shoulder braised for hours in red until the sauce turns to lacquer
dish:Bœuf bourguignon.text: Shoulder braised for hours in red until the sauce turns to lacquer EUR 22-32 WALK-IN Lunch / Dinner Beef shoulder or cheek browned, then braised slowly in red wine with a bouquet garni, lardons, small onions and mushrooms, until the meat yields and the sauce is glossy and dark. The long-cooked sibling of the meurette — same wine, same logic, more time. A dish that wants the afternoon, not the fifteen-minute service. Ma Cuisine is the reference. Where every honest bouchon

dish:Jambon persillé de Bourgogne.name: Jambon persillé de Bourgogne
dish:Jambon persillé de Bourgogne.label: CHARCUTERIE
dish:Jambon persillé de Bourgogne.hook: Ham, tarragon, white wine, parsley jelly — the Easter terrine of Burgundy
dish:Jambon persillé de Bourgogne.text: Ham, tarragon, white wine, parsley jelly — the Easter terrine of Burgundy EUR 5-9 / slice WALK-IN All day Shoulder ham simmered for hours in a court-bouillon with tarragon, thyme and white wine, hand-torn into rough chunks, then set in a terrine in its own parsley-flecked jelly — served cold, sliced thick, with cornichons and mustard. The critic Gilles Pudlowski calls Eddy Raillard 's, on rue Monge, a model of the genre. Traditionally an Easter dish; in Beaune, a year-round one. Where Place Monge charcutiers · the market

dish:Gougères.name: Gougères
dish:Gougères.label: TRADITIONAL
dish:Gougères.hook: Warm cheese choux — the first thing the Côte puts in your hand
dish:Gougères.text: Warm cheese choux — the first thing the Côte puts in your hand EUR 2-5 WALK-IN All day Choux pastry made with Gruyère or Comté, baked into airy golden puffs, served warm. On the Côte d'Or the gougère is not a snack but a ritual: it is what opens every cellar tasting, the savoury bite that resets the palate before the first wine. Bought warm from any good Beaune boulangerie; placed on the table, unasked, at Loiseau des Vignes . Where every boulangerie · every cellar

dish:Escargots de Bourgogne.name: Escargots de Bourgogne
dish:Escargots de Bourgogne.label: TRADITIONAL
dish:Escargots de Bourgogne.hook: Helix pomatia in garlic-parsley butter — scarce, seasonal, worth the question
dish:Escargots de Bourgogne.text: Helix pomatia in garlic-parsley butter — scarce, seasonal, worth the question EUR 14-22 / dozen WALK-IN Dinner The true Burgundy snail — Helix pomatia — baked in its shell under butter creamed with garlic and parsley. Genuine local escargots de Bourgogne are now scarce and seasonal; much of what is sold around the monuments is frozen helix from elsewhere. An honest bouchon will tell you which it is — ask, and order them where the answer is straight, like Ma Cuisine . Where Ma Cuisine · the bouchons

dish:Époisses.name: Époisses
dish:Époisses.label: CHEESE
dish:Époisses.hook: Washed-rind cow's milk, brined and bathed in marc — the pungent one
dish:Époisses.text: Washed-rind cow's milk, brined and bathed in marc — the pungent one EUR 8-14 WALK-IN All day A soft cow's-milk cheese from the village of Époisses, its orange rind washed repeatedly through ageing with brine and marc de Bourgogne until it is gloriously, defiantly strong — the cheese said to have been Napoleon's. The benchmark maker is Berthaut at Époisses; on a Beaune Saturday it reaches the market stalls direct. Eat it with a spoon and a glass of Marc. Where the market · the fromagers

dish:Coq au vin.name: Coq au vin
dish:Coq au vin.label: TRADITIONAL
dish:Coq au vin.hook: Old bird, long braise, a bottle of red — a recipe for using up both
dish:Coq au vin.text: Old bird, long braise, a bottle of red — a recipe for using up both EUR 20-28 WALK-IN Lunch / Dinner A mature rooster — tougher, deeper-flavoured than a young hen — jointed and braised slowly in red wine with lardons, onions and mushrooms, the sauce sometimes bound with the bird's own blood. A peasant economy dish: the wine that was no longer young, the bird that was no longer laying, both made glorious by time. Found on the Burgundian menus, less often than the meurette but worth seeking. Where the bouchons

drink:Pinot Noir — the red of the Côte.name: Pinot Noir — the red of the Côte
drink:Pinot Noir — the red of the Côte.label: WINE
drink:Pinot Noir — the red of the Côte.hook: One grape, several hundred climats, a different wine every hundred metres
drink:Pinot Noir — the red of the Côte.text: One grape, several hundred climats, a different wine every hundred metres EUR 25-200+ / bottle ESSENTIAL at table Dinner The entire red Côte d'Or is a single grape — Pinot Noir — read through several hundred named climats . Beaune's own appellation is overwhelmingly red: Les Grèves, Les Bressandes, Les Teurons, Champs Pimont, the upper-slope premier crus that climb behind the town. The lesson of Burgundy is that the variety is almost a constant and the ground is the variable. Taste it across the Côte by the glass at Loiseau des Vignes . Where Beaune 1er cru · the whole Côte d'Or

drink:Chardonnay — and the Clos des Mouc.name: Chardonnay — and the Clos des Mouches
drink:Chardonnay — and the Clos des Mouc.label: WINE
drink:Chardonnay — and the Clos des Mouc.hook: The white grape of the world's greatest dry whites — Meursault, Puligny, Corton-Charlemagne
drink:Chardonnay — and the Clos des Mouc.text: The white grape of the world's greatest dry whites — Meursault, Puligny, Corton-Charlemagne EUR 30-300+ / bottle ESSENTIAL at table Lunch / Dinner The Côte de Beaune is where Chardonnay became the benchmark white of the planet — Meursault, Puligny-Montrachet, Corton-Charlemagne, all within a short drive south and north of town. Beaune itself makes one celebrated white: the Clos des Mouches , a premier cru owned in its white part by Joseph Drouhin. Buy the village wines at the Saturday market vignerons; taste the crus at the négociant cellars. Where Côte de Beaune

drink:The climat — Beaune's 42 premier c.name: The climat — Beaune's 42 premier crus
drink:The climat — Beaune's 42 premier c.label: TERROIR
drink:The climat — Beaune's 42 premier c.hook: 42 premier crus, zero grand crus — a singular ratio
drink:The climat — Beaune's 42 premier c.text: 42 premier crus, zero grand crus — a singular ratio — — — A climat is a named, mapped parcel of vines with its own history and rank — the unit the Cistercian monks invented by walking the slope for centuries. Beaune's appellation holds 42 of them at premier cru and not a single grand cru: more than three-quarters of the appellation classed at the upper tier, yet no crown. The town put its ambition into the trade. The whole system was inscribed by UNESCO in 2015. Read it at the Cité des Climats et Vins . Where the slope west of the ramparts

drink:Kir — Aligoté & crème de cassis.name: Kir — Aligoté & crème de cassis
drink:Kir — Aligoté & crème de cassis.label: APÉRITIF
drink:Kir — Aligoté & crème de cassis.hook: A measure of cassis, five of cold Aligoté — named for a priest-mayor
drink:Kir — Aligoté & crème de cassis.text: A measure of cassis, five of cold Aligoté — named for a priest-mayor EUR 4-7 WALK-IN Apéritif The Burgundian apéritif: one part crème de cassis under four or five of cold Bourgogne Aligoté, the sharp third white grape whose acidity carries the sweet blackcurrant liqueur. Named for Félix Kir, the Resistance priest and mayor of Dijon from 1945 to 1968, who poured it at every civic reception. Swap the Aligoté for Crémant and it becomes a Kir Royale. The cassis itself has its museum 18 km north, the Cassissium at Nuits-Saint-Georges. Where every café

drink:Crémant de Bourgogne.name: Crémant de Bourgogne
drink:Crémant de Bourgogne.label: SPARKLING
drink:Crémant de Bourgogne.hook: Méthode traditionnelle, AOC since 1975 — Burgundy's everyday bubble
drink:Crémant de Bourgogne.text: Méthode traditionnelle, AOC since 1975 — Burgundy's everyday bubble EUR 12-25 / bottle WALK-IN All day Burgundy's sparkling wine, made by the same bottle-fermented method as Champagne — minimum nine months on the lees — and an AOC in its own right since 1975. Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Aligoté and Gamay are the usual grapes. The honest, unpretentious pour for any hour in Beaune, and the proper base of a Kir Royale. Where every cellar · every list

drink:Marc & Fine de Bourgogne.name: Marc & Fine de Bourgogne
drink:Marc & Fine de Bourgogne.label: SPIRIT
drink:Marc & Fine de Bourgogne.hook: Two Burgundy brandies — one from the pomace, one from the lees
drink:Marc & Fine de Bourgogne.text: Two Burgundy brandies — one from the pomace, one from the lees EUR 6-14 / glass WALK-IN Digestif Marc de Bourgogne is distilled from the pressed grape skins and stalks; Fine de Bourgogne from the wine lees, the sediment left in the barrel — finer, rounder, oak-aged a minimum of three years. Both were raised to full AOC in 2011, set on a par with Cognac and Armagnac. The Marc is also what washes the rind of an Époisses. The digestif to end a Beaune dinner. Where after dinner

drink:Vin Jaune — 75 minutes east.name: Vin Jaune — 75 minutes east
drink:Vin Jaune — 75 minutes east.label: THE JURA BRIDGE
drink:Vin Jaune — 75 minutes east.hook: Cross the rift and the wine changes philosophy entirely
drink:Vin Jaune — 75 minutes east.text: Cross the rift and the wine changes philosophy entirely EUR 35-90 / clavelin — — Drive 107 km east on the A36 and A39 — about 75 minutes — and you cross from Burgundy into the Jura, from one side of the Bressan rift to the other. The same Jurassic geology lifts again into blue marls, and the wine changes its whole creed: Vin Jaune , Savagnin aged six years and three months under a voile of yeast in an unfilled barrel, bottled in the 62 cl clavelin . Where Beaune prizes precision and freshness, Château-Chalon prizes oxidation and patience — a geographical neighbour and a philosophical opposite. The Littoralicious Terroir guide to Lons-le-Saunier & the Jura takes it from there. Where Château-Chalon, Jura — 107 km

music:Festival International d'Opéra Bar.name: Festival International d'Opéra Baroque et Romantique
music:Festival International d'Opéra Bar.label: FESTIVAL
music:Festival International d'Opéra Bar.text: 3–26 July 2026 · 44th edition, themed 'Au-delà' France's premier baroque and romantic opera festival. The 2026 programme spans the Hôtel-Dieu courtyard, the Basilique Notre-Dame, and — new this year — the Beaune Theatre. Confirmed: Handel's Il Trionfo del Tempo e del Disinganno (11 July, Cour de l'Hôtel-Dieu, 21:00); L'Olimpiade (18 July, 21:00); Cantates de l'adieu (26 July, 17:30, Basilique); and, for the first fully staged opera in the festival's history, Gasparini's L'Avare (1720, after Molière), directed by Vincent Dumestre. Tickets open online 10 March 2026. Where Hôtel-Dieu courtyard · Basilique Notre-Dame · Beaune Theatre

music:Rootstock Festival — Château de Po.name: Rootstock Festival — Château de Pommard
music:Rootstock Festival — Château de Po.label: FESTIVAL
music:Rootstock Festival — Château de Po.hook: 14–15 July 2026 · world & soul in a walled vineyard
music:Rootstock Festival — Château de Po.text: 14–15 July 2026 · world & soul in a walled vineyard Two-day festival in the 20-hectare walled vineyard of Château de Pommard , 4 km south of Beaune. 2026 headliners: Fatoumata Diawara (Saturday) and the Cuban-French twin duo Ibeyi — Lisa-Kaindé and Naomi Díaz — (Sunday). Two stages: main stage for the named acts and a scène découverte for emerging artists in the historic gardens; vineyard cycling, wine-and-food pairings and open-air yoga between sets. The closest serious festival to Beaune you can reach on foot from a great Pinot Noir vineyard. Where Pommard — 4 km south of Beaune

music:Dijon — La Vapeur SMAC & Le SIRK F.name: Dijon — La Vapeur SMAC & Le SIRK Festival
music:Dijon — La Vapeur SMAC & Le SIRK F.label: ELECTRONIC
music:Dijon — La Vapeur SMAC & Le SIRK F.hook: La Vapeur (42 av. Stalingrad) · Le SIRK Festival every April
music:Dijon — La Vapeur SMAC & Le SIRK F.text: La Vapeur (42 av. Stalingrad) · Le SIRK Festival every April For an electronic night Beaune cannot give you, drive 45 minutes to Dijon. La Vapeur , the regional SMAC (600 cap., 42 Avenue de Stalingrad), runs the year-round programme — including the SYNC B2B nights showcasing Dijon's electronic collectives and the international L'Extra Festival (7–10 May 2026, lineups from Germany, Algeria, Belgium, Venezuela, Switzerland, Italy, Spain, Colombia, Brazil). The Le SIRK Festival , every April, is the region's major dedicated electronic event — techno, house, ambient, footwork — spread across La Vapeur, the Consortium contemporary-art museum (a Shigeru Ban building) and a former aerodrome. Past lineups: Ellen Allien, Steffi, SHERELLE. Where Dijon — 45 min north

music:Collégiale Notre-Dame — concerts &.name: Collégiale Notre-Dame — concerts & Festival Beethoven
music:Collégiale Notre-Dame — concerts &.label: VENUE
music:Collégiale Notre-Dame — concerts &.hook: A Romanesque nave that doubles as the festival's concert hall
music:Collégiale Notre-Dame — concerts &.text: A Romanesque nave that doubles as the festival's concert hall Beyond the July baroque festival, the 12th-century Collégiale Notre-Dame hosts sacred music and the annual Festival Beethoven in April. The Romanesque acoustics — long, generous, stone — suit early music and string-quartet exactly. The other festival ear-mark: Festival Bélen in June under the direction of André Manoukian, world music and voices, using Notre-Dame, the Parc de la Bouzaise and Place Carnot. Where Place Général Leclerc

music:The cellar-and-counter night.name: The cellar-and-counter night
music:The cellar-and-counter night.label: LATE
music:The cellar-and-counter night.hook: Beaune's evening is a glass and a conversation, not a dancefloor
music:The cellar-and-counter night.text: Beaune's evening is a glass and a conversation, not a dancefloor An honest read: Beaune is a wine town of 22,000, not a club town. The night is the natural-wine counter at Enstase (which opens its concealed kitchen on Thursdays and Fridays for communal bao and gua bao under chef Pierre-Olivier Soares), a wine bar around Place Madeleine, a last glass with someone who can talk you through it. Treat that as the programme, not the shortfall. Where Place Madeleine · Enstase

culture:Hôtel-Dieu — Hospices de Beaune.name: Hôtel-Dieu — Hospices de Beaune
culture:Hôtel-Dieu — Hospices de Beaune.label: MONUMENT
culture:Hôtel-Dieu — Hospices de Beaune.hook: A hospital for the poor, paid for by vines, for 528 years
culture:Hôtel-Dieu — Hospices de Beaune.text: A hospital for the poor, paid for by vines, for 528 years EUR 12.50 WALK-IN Morning Founded in 1443 by Nicolas Rolin, chancellor of Burgundy, and Guigone de Salins, as a free hospital for the poor — and it stayed one until 1971. The roof of glazed polychrome tiles, laid in chevrons of amber, black and green, is the image of Beaune. Inside, the 72-metre Grande Salle des Pôvres keeps its curtained box-beds and its painted vault. The institution still owns 60 hectares of vines and funds itself, in part, by the November auction. Allow 90 minutes; arrive at opening. Where Centre — Place de la Halle

culture:Van der Weyden — The Last Judgme.name: Van der Weyden — The Last Judgment
culture:Van der Weyden — The Last Judgme.label: MASTERPIECE
culture:Van der Weyden — The Last Judgme.hook: Fifteen Flemish panels, weighed souls, gold scales
culture:Van der Weyden — The Last Judgme.text: Fifteen Flemish panels, weighed souls, gold scales included with the Hôtel-Dieu WALK-IN Morning Rolin commissioned the Last Judgment polyptych from Rogier van der Weyden, the supreme Flemish painter of the age, for the hospital's chapel. Fifteen painted panels: Christ enthroned on a rainbow, the Archangel Michael weighing souls in golden scales, the blessed and the damned parting left and right. It still hangs in the Hôtel-Dieu, shown with a magnifying mirror so you can read the faces of the saved and the lost. Where inside the Hôtel-Dieu

culture:Collégiale Notre-Dame.name: Collégiale Notre-Dame
culture:Collégiale Notre-Dame.label: CHURCH
culture:Collégiale Notre-Dame.hook: A Cluniac nave and five tapestries of the Life of the Virgin
chips: free (church) · small fee for the tapestries
culture:Collégiale Notre-Dame.text: A Cluniac nave and five tapestries of the Life of the Virgin free (church) · small fee for the tapestries WALK-IN All day One of the last great Romanesque churches of Burgundy, Cluniac in inspiration, built from the 12th century with Gothic and Renaissance additions. Behind the choir hang the Vie de la Vierge — five Tournai tapestries in wool and silk, completed around 1500, astonishingly preserved. The tapestries show on a restricted schedule (afternoons, April–October); the nave is open and, on a weekday morning, empty. Where Place Général Leclerc

culture:The ramparts of Beaune.name: The ramparts of Beaune
culture:The ramparts of Beaune.label: RAMPARTS
culture:The ramparts of Beaune.hook: A 2.5 km circuit that never lost its towers
culture:The ramparts of Beaune.text: A 2.5 km circuit that never lost its towers free WALK-IN Morning Beaune's medieval wall survives almost whole — a 2.5-kilometre circuit past seventeen towers, bastions and gates, much of it now garden promenade. The Rempart des Dames, a double avenue of plane trees on a bastion of 1637, is the loveliest stretch; the neoclassical Porte Saint-Nicolas (1762–1770) is the surviving gate. Several bastions hold négociant cellars — Chanson's wine sleeps inside a 15th-century tower with ten-metre walls. Where the ring

culture:Cité des Climats et Vins de Bour.name: Cité des Climats et Vins de Bourgogne
culture:Cité des Climats et Vins de Bour.label: MUSEUM
culture:Cité des Climats et Vins de Bour.hook: The terroir made legible — the UNESCO climat system explained
culture:Cité des Climats et Vins de Bour.text: The terroir made legible — the UNESCO climat system explained EUR 12-20 (verify) BOOK-AHEAD All day Opened in spring 2023 in a purpose-built timber spiral at the edge of town, this is the place to understand what a climat actually is before you walk the slope or taste a cru. Interactive exhibitions on the UNESCO landscape, panoramic terraces over the vineyard, wine courses and tastings. Reserve guided visits and tastings ahead. Where 21 avenue Charles de Gaulle

culture:Musée du Vin de Bourgogne.name: Musée du Vin de Bourgogne
culture:Musée du Vin de Bourgogne.label: MUSEUM
culture:Musée du Vin de Bourgogne.hook: Cooperage, presses and the history of the trade — in the Dukes' palace
culture:Musée du Vin de Bourgogne.text: Cooperage, presses and the history of the trade — in the Dukes' palace EUR 6 WALK-IN Afternoon The municipal wine museum occupies the Hôtel des Ducs de Bourgogne, the late-medieval palace of the Dukes — three floors of presses, cooperage tools, documents and the long story of the négoce. An honest flag: the museum has been listed as temporarily closed in early 2026; check its status with the tourist office before walking over. Where Hôtel des Ducs de Bourgogne, rue Paradis

culture:Musée Marey & Musée des Beaux-Ar.name: Musée Marey & Musée des Beaux-Arts
culture:Musée Marey & Musée des Beaux-Ar.label: MUSEUM
culture:Musée Marey & Musée des Beaux-Ar.hook: The Beaune man who photographed motion and pre-figured cinema
culture:Musée Marey & Musée des Beaux-Ar.text: The Beaune man who photographed motion and pre-figured cinema EUR 6 (combined ticket) WALK-IN Afternoon Installed in the bastioned Porte Marie de Bourgogne, the town's museums honour two Beaune-born figures: Félix Ziem, the painter of Venetian light, and Étienne-Jules Marey, the physiologist whose chronophotography — capturing a body or a bird across a single plate — was a direct ancestor of the moving image. A quiet, surprising stop two minutes from the wine streets. Where Porte Marie de Bourgogne, boulevard Perpreuil

work:Parc de la Bouzaise.name: Parc de la Bouzaise
work:Parc de la Bouzaise.label: PARK
work:Parc de la Bouzaise.hook: A 5-hectare English garden five minutes from the cellars
work:Parc de la Bouzaise.text: A 5-hectare English garden five minutes from the cellars Laid out in 1883 in the English manner — winding paths, a small lake with rowing boats, mature specimen trees — the Parc de la Bouzaise is where the noise of the town drops to nothing. On a weekday between 09:00 and 11:00 it is nearly empty. The bench facing the lake, the willows behind, the old spillway just audible: bring the morning's market bread. Where western edge, by Faubourg Bretonnière

work:Cité des Climats — the terraces.name: Cité des Climats — the terraces
work:Cité des Climats — the terraces.label: VIEW
work:Cité des Climats — the terraces.hook: Panoramic terraces over the slope, with a coffee
work:Cité des Climats — the terraces.text: Panoramic terraces over the slope, with a coffee The 2023 Cité des Climats et Vins has open terraces looking straight at the vineyard escarpment — a calm, modern place to sit with a notebook and a coffee, the whole geology of the guide laid out in front of you. Where 21 avenue Charles de Gaulle

work:A Place Carnot terrace.name: A Place Carnot terrace
work:A Place Carnot terrace.label: TERRACE
work:A Place Carnot terrace.hook: The town's living room — café, market overflow, passing trade
work:A Place Carnot terrace.text: The town's living room — café, market overflow, passing trade For people-watching rather than silence: a café terrace on Place Carnot puts you in the middle of Beaune's daily traffic — the market on its edges, the brocante in summer, the whole town crossing the square. Good coffee, and the best free theatre in Beaune. Where Place Carnot

work:Rempart des Dames.name: Rempart des Dames
work:Rempart des Dames.label: PROMENADE
work:Rempart des Dames.hook: A bench under the plane trees, on a 1637 bastion
work:Rempart des Dames.text: A bench under the plane trees, on a 1637 bastion The double avenue of plane trees on the Rempart des Dames is a shaded promenade with benches, the moat below, old towers in view. The place to read or think between visits — cool even in July under the canopy. Where the western ramparts

events:Vente des Vins des Hospices — Les.name: Vente des Vins des Hospices — Les Trois Glorieuses
events:Vente des Vins des Hospices — Les.label: AUCTION
events:Vente des Vins des Hospices — Les.text: 13–16 November 2026 · the 166th charity wine auction The world's most famous charity wine auction, held since 1859 on the third Sunday of November. The 166th edition falls on Sunday 15 November 2026 , in the Halles de Beaune, run with Sotheby's since 2021. It anchors Les Trois Glorieuses : Friday 13 Nov , the 153rd Fête des Grands Vins de Bourgogne at the Palais des Congrès (public tasting of all Burgundy appellations); Saturday 14 Nov , the Chapitre des Chevaliers du Tastevin at Clos de Vougeot (the Confrérie was founded in 1934 in the depths of the Depression by négociants Georges Faiveley and Camille Rodier to revive Burgundy's market) + the Vente des Vins semi-marathon + the Festivinales street programme (folk parades, light projections on seven city monuments, gastronomic village on Place Carnot); Sunday 15 Nov , the auction itself, with the Pièce des Présidents sold by candlelight (in 2025 it took €400,000 to a Chinese buyer); Monday 16 Nov , La Paulée de Meursault — a village lunch where every guest brings a bottle to share at table. 2026 charitable cause: rare diseases.

events:Festival International d'Opéra Ba.name: Festival International d'Opéra Baroque
events:Festival International d'Opéra Ba.label: FESTIVAL
events:Festival International d'Opéra Ba.text: 3–26 July 2026 · 44th edition, 'Au-delà' Three weeks of baroque and romantic opera in the Hôtel-Dieu courtyard, the Basilique Notre-Dame and the Beaune Theatre. The 2026 edition stages, for the first time in 44 years, a fully staged opera — Gasparini's L'Avare (1720), directed by Vincent Dumestre. Tickets open online 10 March 2026.

events:Rootstock Festival — Château de P.name: Rootstock Festival — Château de Pommard
events:Rootstock Festival — Château de P.label: FESTIVAL
events:Rootstock Festival — Château de P.hook: 14–15 July 2026 · world & soul in a Pinot Noir vineyard
events:Rootstock Festival — Château de P.text: 14–15 July 2026 · world & soul in a Pinot Noir vineyard Two-day festival 4 km south in the 20-hectare walled vineyard of Château de Pommard. 2026 headliners: Fatoumata Diawara (Saturday) and Ibeyi (Sunday). Two stages, vineyard cycling, food pairings, open-air yoga between sets. The closest thing Beaune has to a music festival you can reach on foot from a great vineyard.

events:Festival de Bach à Bacchus — Meur.name: Festival de Bach à Bacchus — Meursault
events:Festival de Bach à Bacchus — Meur.label: FESTIVAL
events:Festival de Bach à Bacchus — Meur.text: 4–12 July 2026 · 40th anniversary edition Nine days of classical music + Burgundy wine, in the cellars, gardens and church of Meursault. 2026 highlights: Les Divertissements chamber choir (5 July); Mariana Flores in Muse e sirene , 17th-century female composers with Cappella Mediterranea (6 July); a 40th-anniversary carte blanche to Yves Henry with Orchestre de Paris musicians (7 July); Ensemble Alkymia in Bolivian music (9 July). Plus cellar visits with tastings and a theatrical vineyard walk, La clé des sols, à la recherche du pinot perdu .

events:Festival Bélen.name: Festival Bélen
events:Festival Bélen.label: FESTIVAL
events:Festival Bélen.hook: June 2026 · 3rd edition · directed by André Manoukian
events:Festival Bélen.text: June 2026 · 3rd edition · directed by André Manoukian World music and "voices of the world," artistic direction André Manoukian. Venues: the Collégiale Notre-Dame, the Parc de la Bouzaise, Place Carnot, the Théâtre de Verdure. Programme published nearer the date — check belenfestival.com.

events:Art In Situ — Route des Grands Cr.name: Art In Situ — Route des Grands Crus
events:Art In Situ — Route des Grands Cr.label: ART
events:Art In Situ — Route des Grands Cr.text: 7 March – 15 December 2026 · 5th edition Forty-three contemporary artworks by twenty artists placed across nine wine-estate sites along the Route des Grands Crus between Dijon and Beaune — an open-air contemporary art circuit embedded in working vineyard sites, with around two million visitors a year. Free to walk.

events:The Saturday market.name: The Saturday market
events:The Saturday market.label: WEEKLY
events:The Saturday market.hook: Every Saturday, 07:00–13:00 · Place de la Halle & Place Fleury
events:The Saturday market.text: Every Saturday, 07:00–13:00 · Place de la Halle & Place Fleury A fixed star of the Beaune week — around 180 stalls across Place de la Halle, Place Fleury and the covered halls; producers down from the hill villages with cheese, charcuterie, mushrooms, honey, and wine, plus a Fallot mustard stand. The smaller, food-only Wednesday market (07:00–12:30, ~25 merchants) is the quieter alternative.

events:Flowering on the Côte.name: Flowering on the Côte
events:Flowering on the Côte.label: THE VINE YEAR
events:Flowering on the Côte.hook: Late May into June · the slope sets its harvest
events:Flowering on the Côte.text: Late May into June · the slope sets its harvest Not an organised event — a natural one worth timing a visit to. In the last days of May and into June the vines flower on the slope; roughly a hundred days later they are picked. The escarpment is at its greenest, the cellars are between seasons, and Beaune is briefly, genuinely quiet.

walks:The ramparts circuit.name: The ramparts circuit
walks:The ramparts circuit.label: CIRCUIT
walks:The ramparts circuit.hook: 2.5 km · 1-2 hours · 17 numbered towers and bastions
walks:The ramparts circuit.text: 2.5 km · 1-2 hours · 17 numbered towers and bastions The complete medieval wall, walkable almost without a break — 2.5 kilometres past seventeen towers and bastions, much of it garden promenade. Start anywhere; the tourist office on Place de la Halle gives out the map. Walk it at first light from the Rempart des Dames and you will pass nobody. Guided tours July–October open towers normally closed.

walks:Up into the climats.name: Up into the climats
walks:Up into the climats.label: VINEYARD
walks:Up into the climats.hook: 2-3 hours · from the Parc de la Bouzaise into Clos des Mouches & Les Grèves
walks:Up into the climats.text: 2-3 hours · from the Parc de la Bouzaise into Clos des Mouches & Les Grèves From the Parc de la Bouzaise, take the vineyard lanes west — the Chemin de Battaut, then north — and within 200 metres you are inside the premier crus: Clos des Mouches first, then climbing to Les Grèves on the upper slope. From the top of the chemin the whole Côte de Beaune opens below. No other wine capital lets you walk from a town park into a great vineyard in five minutes.

walks:Beaune to Meursault by the vines.name: Beaune to Meursault by the vines
walks:Beaune to Meursault by the vines.label: HALF-DAY
walks:Beaune to Meursault by the vines.text: ~13 km · 3-3.5 hours · Pommard, Volnay, Meursault The classic Route des Grands Crus walk south: out through Beaune's premier crus into Pommard — the Clos des Épeneaux, the village church — then up to Volnay, perched high and famous for finesse, and down through Monthélie to Meursault, the capital of white Burgundy. Return by bus or taxi if you do not walk back.

walks:Corton hill from Pernand-Vergeless.name: Corton hill from Pernand-Vergelesses
walks:Corton hill from Pernand-Vergeless.label: VIEW
walks:Corton hill from Pernand-Vergeless.hook: 6.2 km · 2 hours · the Panorama de la Vierge
walks:Corton hill from Pernand-Vergeless.text: 6.2 km · 2 hours · the Panorama de la Vierge Twelve kilometres north of Beaune, a 6-kilometre loop from the hilltop village of Pernand-Vergelesses climbs through the Corton grand cru — the great wooded dome that carries both a red grand cru and the white Corton-Charlemagne — to the Panorama de la Vierge, with the whole Côte de Beaune below.

walks:The Parc de la Bouzaise loop.name: The Parc de la Bouzaise loop
walks:The Parc de la Bouzaise loop.label: SHORT
walks:The Parc de la Bouzaise loop.hook: 30 minutes · the English garden and the stream
walks:The Parc de la Bouzaise loop.text: 30 minutes · the English garden and the stream A short, gentle loop for an off-hour — the 1883 English garden on the town's western fringe, the lake, the willows, the Bouzaise stream along the western edge. Five minutes from the shopping streets and a different soundscape entirely.

secret-gems:The Hôtel-Dieu courtyard — 0.name: The Hôtel-Dieu courtyard — 09:00
secret-gems:The Hôtel-Dieu courtyard — 0.label: GEM
secret-gems:The Hôtel-Dieu courtyard — 0.text: The Hôtel-Dieu opens at 09:00. For the first half-hour, before the tour groups, the inner courtyard is almost empty — stand in the centre and watch the glazed roof change as the morning sun moves across the tiles. Buy the ticket and go straight to the courtyard; it is a different building by noon. Where Centre When 09:00-09:40, at opening

secret-gems:Rempart des Dames — first li.name: Rempart des Dames — first light
secret-gems:Rempart des Dames — first li.label: GEM
secret-gems:Rempart des Dames — first li.text: The double avenue of plane trees on the 1637 bastion can be walked at first light with nobody on it — the canopy a green vault, old towers showing on the moat side that you never see from inside the town. Come before the bread is out. Where the western ramparts When 06:30-07:30, before the boulangeries open

secret-gems:The lake bench, Parc de la B.name: The lake bench, Parc de la Bouzaise
secret-gems:The lake bench, Parc de la B.label: GEM
secret-gems:The lake bench, Parc de la B.text: After the dawn dog-walkers and before lunch, the 1883 English garden is empty. The bench facing the small lake, willows behind, the old stone spillway audible but out of sight, is the most peaceful seat in Beaune. Bring the morning's market bread. Where western edge When weekday 09:00-11:00

secret-gems:Collégiale Notre-Dame — a we.name: Collégiale Notre-Dame — a weekday morning
secret-gems:Collégiale Notre-Dame — a we.label: GEM
secret-gems:Collégiale Notre-Dame — a we.text: Outside the tapestry-viewing hours the Romanesque church is essentially empty on a weekday morning — the long stone nave in natural light, no groups, no audio guide. The small 12th-century Black Madonna in the choir is unspectacular by tourist measure, and the more affecting for it. Where Place Général Leclerc When Tuesday or Thursday, mid-morning

secret-gems:Rue d'Enfer at dusk.name: Rue d'Enfer at dusk
secret-gems:Rue d'Enfer at dusk.label: GEM
secret-gems:Rue d'Enfer at dusk.text: Beaune's inner streets have names that say what they are: rue Paradis, rue d'Enfer — Hell Street, the coldest in town, because the wine cellars beneath regulate it. At dusk on a weekday it is deserted; the venting slats breathe cool air even in July. The sound of wine resting underground is the silence you hear. Where the cellar streets When 19:00-20:00 on a weekday

secret-gems:Marché aux Vins at opening —.name: Marché aux Vins at opening — 10:00
secret-gems:Marché aux Vins at opening —.label: GEM
secret-gems:Marché aux Vins at opening —.text: The former Cordeliers church takes its first visitors at 10:00 into cool stone chapels with almost nobody else present. The self-guided tasting circuit can be walked in 45 minutes at that hour in something close to silence — five wines, three intact Gothic chapels, the day not yet arrived. Where Centre When 10:00 on a weekday

street-food:Warm gougères from the boula.name: Warm gougères from the boulangerie
street-food:Warm gougères from the boula.label: STREET FOOD
street-food:Warm gougères from the boula.text: The cheese choux puff, bought warm by the bag from a good Beaune boulangerie — the regional grab-and-go, the same thing every cellar hands you at a tasting. Eat them while they are still warm, walking the ramparts. Where any good boulangerie When morning, from the oven

street-food:Jambon persillé by the slice.name: Jambon persillé by the slice — Raillard
street-food:Jambon persillé by the slice.label: STREET FOOD
street-food:Jambon persillé by the slice.text: A thick slice of jambon persillé from Charcuterie Raillard or Franck Bourgeon on Place Monge, with bread from next door and a cornichon, is the most Burgundian lunch you can eat standing up. Pudlowski's benchmark for the dish. Where rue Monge / Place Monge When shop hours · Saturday market

street-food:The Saturday-market traiteur.name: The Saturday-market traiteur
street-food:The Saturday-market traiteur.label: STREET FOOD
street-food:The Saturday-market traiteur.text: On Saturday a rotating traiteur at the market sells hot snails in garlic butter, roast chicken and Burgundian plats to eat then and there — the closest Beaune comes to street food, and only as good as the morning's stall. Go early. Where Place de la Halle When Saturday 08:00-13:00

gastronomy:Marché des Halles — Saturday.name: Marché des Halles — Saturday
gastronomy:Marché des Halles — Saturday.label: MARKET
gastronomy:Marché des Halles — Saturday.text: Saturday 07:00-13:00 · ~180 stalls The big market — producers from the hill villages with Époisses and Cîteaux cheese, jambon persillé, charcuterie, honey, autumn mushrooms, flowers and wine, plus the Fallot mustard stand. Arrive before 10:00 for the producers; the covered halls themselves are worth the walk. Where Place de la Halle, Place Fleury, the covered halls

gastronomy:The Wednesday market.name: The Wednesday market
gastronomy:The Wednesday market.label: MARKET
gastronomy:The Wednesday market.text: Wednesday morning · food only, ~25 stalls The smaller mid-week market — food and table goods only, quieter, more local. The better option for a calm morning shop without the Saturday crowd. Where Place de la Halle

gastronomy:Edmond Fallot — La Moutarderi.name: Edmond Fallot — La Moutarderie
gastronomy:Edmond Fallot — La Moutarderi.label: MUSTARD
gastronomy:Edmond Fallot — La Moutarderi.hook: Burgundy's last independent family mustard mill
gastronomy:Edmond Fallot — La Moutarderi.text: Burgundy's last independent family mustard mill Founded in 1840 by Léon Bouley, a miller who began producing mustard from Burgundian sénevé seeds. In 1928 it was bought by Edmond Fallot (a Doubs-born papermaker and World-War-I veteran) who renamed it and committed to preserving the granite-stone-mill technique. Today the house is run by Marc Désarménien, Edmond's grandson — the last independent family moutarderie in Burgundy, milling about 2,500 tonnes a year on granite millstones near 770 kg each. The slow stone grind keeps the paste cool and the volatile aromatics intact, a method industry abandoned. The tour shows the millstones at work; the Enjoy Fallot boutique sells the full range. A Fallot stand sits at the Saturday market. Where 31 rue du Faubourg Bretonnière Address 31 rue du Faubourg Bretonnière, 21200 Beaune Phone +33 3 80 22 10 02

gastronomy:Charcuterie Raillard.name: Charcuterie Raillard
gastronomy:Charcuterie Raillard.label: CHARCUTERIE
gastronomy:Charcuterie Raillard.hook: Jambon persillé called a model of the genre
gastronomy:Charcuterie Raillard.text: Jambon persillé called a model of the genre Eddy Raillard's charcuterie on rue Monge is, in the words of the critic Gilles Pudlowski, a model of the genre for jambon persillé — the parsley-flecked Burgundian ham terrine — and the place also turns out gougères and pâté en croûte. The rue/Place Monge corner is the artisan-charcutier quarter of Beaune; Franck Bourgeon, a few doors on at 9 Place Monge, holds the same standard. Where 4 rue Monge Address 4 rue Monge, 21200 Beaune

gastronomy:Fromagerie Berthaut — Époisse.name: Fromagerie Berthaut — Époisses
gastronomy:Fromagerie Berthaut — Époisse.label: CHEESE
gastronomy:Fromagerie Berthaut — Époisse.hook: The benchmark maker of AOP Époisses
gastronomy:Fromagerie Berthaut — Époisse.text: The benchmark maker of AOP Époisses In the village of Époisses, two hours north-west, the Berthaut family makes the benchmark AOP Époisses — the washed-rind, marc-bathed cow's-milk cheese at the pungent edge of the law — plus Soumaintrain and Affidélice. Too far for a casual trip, but the cheese itself reaches the Beaune Saturday market direct. Closed Sundays. Where Époisses — ~86 km / 2 h from Beaune Address rue du Champ de Foire, 21460 Époisses Phone +33 3 80 96 39 19

gastronomy:Fromage de Cîteaux — Abbaye d.name: Fromage de Cîteaux — Abbaye de Cîteaux
gastronomy:Fromage de Cîteaux — Abbaye d.label: CHEESE
gastronomy:Fromage de Cîteaux — Abbaye d.hook: A washed-rind disc made by Cistercian monks
gastronomy:Fromage de Cîteaux — Abbaye d.text: A washed-rind disc made by Cistercian monks At the mother abbey of the Cistercian order — founded 1098 — the monks still make the cheese of Cîteaux: a soft, washed-rind disc from the raw milk of their own Montbéliarde herd, sold only at the abbey shop and a few fromagers. Half an hour north of Beaune, easily folded into a Côte de Nuits day. The abbey is a working monastery — silence and respect are expected. Where Saint-Nicolas-lès-Cîteaux — ~25 km north Address Abbaye de Cîteaux, 21700 Saint-Nicolas-lès-Cîteaux Phone +33 3 80 61 11 53

gastronomy:Mulot & Petitjean.name: Mulot & Petitjean
gastronomy:Mulot & Petitjean.label: PAIN D'ÉPICES
gastronomy:Mulot & Petitjean.hook: Burgundy pain d'épices — a house founded in Dijon in 1796
gastronomy:Mulot & Petitjean.text: Burgundy pain d'épices — a house founded in Dijon in 1796 The Beaune boutique of the Dijon pain d'épices house Mulot & Petitjean, founded 1796 and carrying the Living Heritage Company label. Traditional spice bread, nonnettes — small glazed spice cakes filled with jam — all made by hand. The Burgundian thing to bring home, and the classic partner to foie gras or a strong cheese. Where 1 Place Carnot Address 1 Place Carnot, 21200 Beaune

gastronomy:Athenaeum de la Vigne et du V.name: Athenaeum de la Vigne et du Vin
gastronomy:Athenaeum de la Vigne et du V.label: BOOKS & WINE
gastronomy:Athenaeum de la Vigne et du V.hook: A bookshop entirely about wine, beside the Hospices
gastronomy:Athenaeum de la Vigne et du V.text: A bookshop entirely about wine, beside the Hospices Next to the Hôtel-Dieu, the Athenaeum is a bookshop and wine-culture shop devoted to the vine — maps of the climats, the standard references, glassware, tastevins, cellar tools. The place to buy the map that makes the slope legible before you walk it. Where by the Hôtel-Dieu Address near the Hôtel-Dieu, 21200 Beaune

gastronomy:Fromagerie Alain Hess.name: Fromagerie Alain Hess
gastronomy:Fromagerie Alain Hess.label: FROMAGER
gastronomy:Fromagerie Alain Hess.text: The town fromager and fine-grocer On Place Carnot, Alain Hess is the destination fromagerie and fine-grocer of central Beaune — aged cheeses, the regional charcuterie including jambon persillé, and the curiosity that made the house known, the Délice de Pommard, a fresh cheese rolled in mustard seed. Where to assemble a picnic for the Parc de la Bouzaise. Where Place Carnot Address Place Carnot, 21200 Beaune

avoid:Burgundy by the glass on a tourist.name: Burgundy by the glass on a tourist terrace
avoid:Burgundy by the glass on a tourist.label: AVOID
avoid:Burgundy by the glass on a tourist.hook: Place Carnot café terraces — the négoce's most anonymous cuvée at a markup
avoid:Burgundy by the glass on a tourist.text: Place Carnot café terraces — the négoce's most anonymous cuvée at a markup The big café terraces pour the most generic regional Bourgogne by the glass at a tourist price, and call it the experience. The wine that explains the slope is tasted in a cellar, with someone who made or chose it — at Marché aux Vins , at Enstase , or on a négociant visit. Use the terrace for a coffee and the view, not for your impression of Burgundy.

avoid:The frozen-snail tourist menu.name: The frozen-snail tourist menu
avoid:The frozen-snail tourist menu.label: AVOID
avoid:The frozen-snail tourist menu.hook: The 'menu escargots' clustered around the Hôtel-Dieu
avoid:The frozen-snail tourist menu.text: The 'menu escargots' clustered around the Hôtel-Dieu Several menus around the monuments sell frozen helix from elsewhere, drowned in industrial garlic butter, as 'escargots de Bourgogne'. True local Burgundy snails are scarce and seasonal. An honest bouchon — Ma Cuisine , Le Conty — will tell you straight which it is serving. Ask the question.

avoid:Arriving for a quiet day on auctio.name: Arriving for a quiet day on auction Sunday
avoid:Arriving for a quiet day on auctio.label: AVOID
avoid:Arriving for a quiet day on auctio.hook: The third Sunday of November — the Vente des Vins
avoid:Arriving for a quiet day on auctio.text: The third Sunday of November — the Vente des Vins If you want Beaune calm, do not come on the third Sunday of November. That is the Vente des Vins weekend — the town's loudest, with the auction in the Halles, projections on the monuments, crowds in every street. Magnificent, but the opposite of the quiet this guide is built around. Come for the auction deliberately, or avoid that weekend deliberately.

avoid:Driving the Route des Grands Crus.name: Driving the Route des Grands Crus and tasting
avoid:Driving the Route des Grands Crus.label: AVOID
avoid:Driving the Route des Grands Crus.hook: Cellar visits, a car, and France's drink-drive limit
avoid:Driving the Route des Grands Crus.text: Cellar visits, a car, and France's drink-drive limit It is tempting to drive Pommard–Volnay–Meursault and taste at each. France's limit is low and the gendarmerie know the season. Either walk the vineyard route, hire a driver or a cycling tour, or appoint one taster who stays dry. The wine will keep; the licence might not.
